before.html:
Question 2
?

Find the slope of the normal line to the curve y=x3−4x5 at the point (1,−3).

a
−17
b
7
c
−1
d
−7
e
17
Submit

decision.explanation: Write y=x^3-4x^{5/2}. Then y'=3x^2-10x^{3/2}, so the tangent slope at x=1 is -7. The normal slope is its negative reciprocal, 1/7.

after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}-4\sqrt{{x}^{5}}.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-4\sqrt{{x}^{5}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-4{x}^{5/2}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}-10{x}^{3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=3(1)^{2}-10(1)^{3/2}=-7\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line  ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{7}.
$$

Question 1
?

Find the slope of the normal line to the curve y=x2+x at the point (1,2).

a
13
b
12
c
−13
d
−1
e
−12
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative is y'=2x+1, so the tangent slope at x=1 is 3. The normal slope is its negative reciprocal, -1/3.

after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}+x.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+x) \\  & =2x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,2):$

$$
m={f}^{′}(1)=2(1)+1=3
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms that f'(1)=2(1)+1=3. The normal slope is the negative reciprocal, -1/3, matching option c. The submitted option d, -1, is incorrect.
